name: Microsoft Azure ND H200 v5 (ND96isr, 8x H200)
region: eastus2, westus2 and ~30 regions (westus3 lists $110.24, usgovvirginia $106.00)
price_basis: per H200 GPU-hour. ND96isr H200 v5 = 8x H200, on-demand $84.80/instance-hr / 8 = $10.60 in eastus2 and westus2. Reservation $407,526/h normalised (1yr) and $1,109,592/h (3yr). Low Priority $16.96 in eastus2. Fetched from the Retail Prices API 2026-10-03.
notes: THE STRONGEST AVAILABILITY SIGNAL IN THE SLICE, and the reason this record exists. Azure Spot for H200 v5 is published at EXACTLY $84.80 - byte-identical to the on-demand rate, i.e. a 0% discount. Every other SKUs in this record set publishes a spot rate meaningfully below on-demand. A zero-discount spot price is what a sold-out fleet looks like in a price API. Separately, the Azure pricing web page refuses to quote this series at all in the selected region ('Pricing is not available in the selected region'), so the API is the only place the number exists. On price, $10.60/H200-hour sits between Google a3-ultragpu ($10.60, identical) and AWS p5en ($7.91), and above the AWS p5e Capacity Block rate ($5.97). Egress is billed separately and there is no credit-card-free path. Note the H200 series also has no savings plan published, only the normalised Reservation meters.
